+# Case study: issue #335 — sync stability fixes from upstream OpenCode
+
+Issue: https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/335
+Pull request: https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/pull/339
+
+## 1. The issue
+
+> We also need to include all code that increases reliability of our code from
+> https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode, so we use all the best practices from
+> there, but with no support for additional tools, only fixing existing tools
+> if we have potential issues.
+
+The issue was opened on 2026-10-22 by konard. It had no comments when this work
+was done.
+
+### 1.1 Requirements
+
+| #   | Requirement (from the issue text)                                              | Where it is handled                            |
+| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
+| R1  | Include upstream code that increases the reliability of our code               | §4–§6, commits in PR #339                      |
+| R2  | Use upstream best practices                                                    | §3 (method), §7 (practices adopted)            |
+| R3  | Do **not** add support for additional tools                                    | §2.3 — no tool was registered or added         |
+| R4  | Only fix existing tools where we have potential issues                         | §4–§5: every port is a fix to an existing tool |
+| R5  | Collect the data related to the issue into `./docs/case-studies/issue-335`     | `data/`, `analysis/`                           |
+| R6  | Do a deep case study analysis, including online research for additional facts  | this file, `analysis/*.md`, §8                 |
+| R7  | List each and all requirements from the issue                                  | this table                                     |
+| R8  | Propose possible solutions and a solution plan for each requirement            | §4–§6 (per-defect solution + status)           |
+| R9  | Check known existing components/libraries that solve or help solve the problem | §9                                             |
+| R10 | Plan and execute everything in this single pull request                        | PR #339                                        |
+
+## 2. Context and timeline
+
+### 2.1 Where the fork comes from
+
+| Date       | Event                                                                                                    |
+| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| 2025-11-19 | Fork base: upstream commit `0068cb305f`. Our `js/` tree is a copy of `packages/opencode` from that time. |
+| 2025-12-15 | Upstream #4388 adds a per-file lock to `edit` (read-before-write race).                                  |
+| 2026-03-07 | Upstream #9443 preserves CRLF line endings in `edit`.                                                    |
+| 2026-03-16 | Upstream #17835 replaces the wall-clock read time with an `{mtime, size}` stamp.                         |
+| 2026-04-01 | Upstream #20367 normalizes paths used as FileTime keys.                                                  |
+| 2026-04-16 | Upstream #22999 deletes the FileTime module (moved into the Effect-based tool runtime).                  |
+| 2026-04-20 | Upstream #23483 re-adds per-file edit locking after the Effect refactor.                                 |
+| 2026-04-22 | Upstream #23797 preserves the UTF-8 BOM in text tool round-trips.                                        |
+| 2026-06-05 | Upstream #30932 stops destructive fuzzy edit matches.                                                    |
+| 2026-07-20 | Upstream `44b6938b2a` deletes `packages/opencode`; the code now lives in `packages/core`.                |
+| 2026-10-12 | Upstream #53166 preserves mixed line endings in `edit`.                                                  |
+| 2026-10-22 | Upstream HEAD `d93568f334` (last tag `github-v1.2.27`). Issue #335 opened.                               |
+
+Because upstream reorganised the code base twice (Effect services, then the
+move from `packages/opencode` to `packages/core`), no upstream commit can be
+cherry-picked. Every fix was re-implemented on our code, with a test that
+fails before the change.
+
+### 2.2 Our two implementations
+
+- `js/` (Bun, TypeScript) — the primary implementation, close to the upstream
+  code from 2025-11.
+- `rust/` — a port of the same tools. Where a defect also exists there, it is
+  fixed there too.
+
+### 2.3 Scope decisions
+
+- **No new tools (R3).** Upstream added tools after the fork point that we do
+  not have (`apply_patch`, `lsp`, `question`, `skill`, `plan-enter`,
+  `plan-exit`, `code-mode`). None were added. The JS
+  `patch` and `multiedit` tools exist in the tree but stay unregistered, as
+  before.
+- **Write keeps "no restrictions".** Upstream `write` requires a prior read.
+  The fork deliberately removed that requirement (commit `db682c8`), so it was
+  not re-added. Write now _records_ a read, so an `edit` right after a `write`
+  works, and it takes the same per-file lock as `edit`.
+- **Session/provider/MCP fixes** are applied only where they fix behaviour of
+  code we already have (see §6).
+
+## 3. Method
+
+1. Cloned upstream and listed every commit after the fork base whose subject
+   starts with `fix` and that touches tools, session, provider or MCP code:
+   900 commits in total (`data/upstream-fix-commits-*.txt`):
+
+   | Area     | Fix commits |
+   | -------- | ----------- |
+   | tools    | 217         |
+   | session  | 399         |
+   | provider | 206         |
+   | mcp      | 78          |
+
+2. Triaged each commit as **PORT** (the defect exists in our code),
+   **ALREADY-HAVE** (we already behave correctly) or **N/A** (the code or
+   feature does not exist here, or it is a UI/infra change). The triage
+   reports are in `analysis/`.
+3. For each PORT item: reproduce with a test or an experiment
+   (`experiments/issue-335/`), apply the fix, and check that the test passes.
+4. Run the whole JS and Rust test suites, lint and format checks.
+
+## 4. Edit and write tools (report A)
+
+Full report: [`analysis/A-edit-write-patch.md`](analysis/A-edit-write-patch.md).
+Reproductions: [`experiments/issue-335/edit-write/`](../../../experiments/issue-335/edit-write/).
+Tests: `js/tests/edit-write-reliability.ts`, `rust/tests/tool_edit.rs`,
+`rust/tests/tool_write.rs`.
+
+| Defect (before)                                                                                  | Upstream         | Fix                                                                                                               | JS  | Rust                             |
+| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | -------------------------------- |
+| Parallel edits of one file read the same content; the last write won and other edits were lost   | #4388, #23483    | `FileTime.withLock` serializes read-modify-write per normalized path; `edit` and `write` both take it             | ✅  | — (no session; calls sequential) |
+| Block-anchor fuzzy match accepted **any** block whose first and last lines matched               | #30932           | Similarity thresholds 0.0/0.3 → 0.65; block size must be within 25 % of `oldString`; disproportionate-match guard | ✅  | ✅                               |
+| Empty `oldString` on an existing file silently replaced the whole file                           | #30932           | Rejected with an explicit error; still allowed for creating a new file                                            | ✅  | ✅                               |
+| `replace(content, '', …)` looped forever                                                         | (found here)     | `replace()` rejects an empty `oldString`                                                                          | ✅  | ✅                               |
+| CRLF files: LF `oldString` did not match, or the edited part was written with LF                 | #9443            | `oldString`/`newString` converted to the file's line ending                                                       | ✅  | ✅                               |
+| Mixed-ending files: one CRLF anywhere made all inserted lines CRLF; Rust rewrote untouched lines | #53166           | Dominant line ending for new lines; Rust maps the result back line by line                                        | ✅  | ✅                               |
+| Rust: fuzzy matches on CRLF files reported success but did not change the file                   | (found here)     | Replacers run on the LF view; endings restored afterwards                                                         | —   | ✅                               |
+| UTF-8 BOM dropped by `edit` and `write`                                                          | #23797           | `Bom` helper splits/re-adds the BOM; no double BOM                                                                | ✅  | ✅                               |
+| `replaceAll` treated `$&`, `$1`, `$'` in `newString` as patterns                                 | (String#replace) | `split/join` instead of `String#replaceAll`                                                                       | ✅  | already literal                  |
+| "Modified since read" false positives for files with a future mtime; misses within the same ms   | #17835           | FileTime stores an `{mtime, size}` stamp and compares for equality                                                | ✅  | — (no FileTime)                  |
+| `dir/./a.txt` and `dir/a.txt` were different FileTime keys                                       | #20367           | Keys normalized with `path.resolve` + `realpath`                                                                  | ✅  | — (no FileTime)                  |
+| `edit` right after `write` failed with "You must read the file"                                  | —                | `write` records a read                                                                                            | ✅  | — (no FileTime)                  |
+| Empty output after a successful edit/write confused some models                                  | `66f9bdab32`     | "Edit applied successfully." / "Wrote file successfully."                                                         | ✅  | ✅                               |
+
+## 5. Read/search and bash/web tools (reports B and C)
+
+Full reports: [`analysis/B-read-search.md`](analysis/B-read-search.md),
+[`analysis/C-bash-web.md`](analysis/C-bash-web.md).
+
+Reproductions: [`experiments/issue-335/read-search/`](../../../experiments/issue-335/read-search/),
+[`experiments/issue-335/bash-web/`](../../../experiments/issue-335/bash-web/).

+`js/tests/read-search-reliability-search.ts`,
+`js/tests/bash-web-reliability.ts`, `rust/tests/tool_{read,grep,glob,bash,webfetch,websearch}.rs`.
+
+### 5.1 Read, grep, glob, ls

+### 6.4 Not ported and known remaining issues
+
+- Upstream replays the user message that overflowed once compaction is done.
+  Here the existing compaction flow is kept: the summary covers the request,
+  and a synthetic "Continue if you have next steps" message resumes the turn.
+- When a model overflows, the compaction model cascade does not move on to
+  the next model; the overflow is reported instead.
+
+## 7. Upstream practices adopted
+
+- Every fix has a regression test that fails without it.
+- File mutations are serialized per canonical path; tool calls of one step and
+  `batch` run concurrently, so this is required for correctness.
+- File identity is the canonical path (`realpath`), not the string the model
+  sent.
+- "Modified since read" is decided by comparing file stamps for equality,
+  never by comparing clocks.
+- Fuzzy matching is bounded: it must not be able to replace text that is much
+  larger than, or very different from, what the model asked to replace.
+- Round-trips keep the file's bytes: BOM and line endings are preserved, and
+  untouched lines are never rewritten.
+- Tools return a short confirmation instead of an empty string.
+- Every external call has a deadline and is cancelled on abort: rg, web
+  requests, MCP connect, `tools/list` and tool calls. A timeout that only
+  rejects the promise is not enough; the request itself is aborted.
+- Loops driven by remote data are bounded (MCP pagination, retry delays).
+- Child processes are cleaned up on every exit path, including grandchildren.
+- Errors are classified by structure first (status code, error code), then by
+  message patterns, and only overflow and transient errors are acted on.
+- Messages sent to a provider are sanitized for what that provider rejects
+  (lone surrogates, empty blocks, foreign signatures).
+
+## 8. Online research
+
+- **Line endings in agent edit tools are a common failure.** Public bug
+  reports for other coding agents describe the same three symptoms we fixed:
+  `oldString` not matching on CRLF files because the read output is
+  LF-normalized, unrelated lines being converted from CRLF to LF, and false
+  "file modified" errors from comparing LF and CRLF versions. See for example
+  the Claude Code reports mirrored at
+  [claudeissues.com #62713](https://claudeissues.com/issue/62713-bug-built-in-edit-tool-silently-converts-line-endings-crlf-lf-in-unrelated-lines),
+  [#54876](https://claudeissues.com/issue/54876-bug-edit-tool-fails-on-windows-with-crlf-line-endings-read-output-mismatches-fil),
+  [#64599](https://claudeissues.com/issue/64599-bug-edit-raises-file-has-been-unexpectedly-modified-on-crlf-files-write-silently)
+  and the Cursor thread
+  [Cursor converts line endings on Windows](https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-converts-line-endings-on-windows/150424).
+- **UTF-8 BOM.** `TextDecoder` strips a leading BOM unless `ignoreBOM: true`
+  is passed. The `ignoreBOM` default is `false`, as the web-platform test
+  [textdecoder-ignorebom](https://cobalt.googlesource.com/cobalt/+/master%5E/third_party/web_platform_tests/encoding/textdecoder-ignorebom.html)
+  checks. The 2012 WHATWG discussion
+  ([thread](https://lists.whatwg.org/pipermail/whatwg-whatwg.org/2012-August/079197.html))
+  notes that Windows tools use the BOM to tell UTF-8 from the legacy code
+  page, so dropping it on write-back can change how a file is read. This is
+  why `Bom.readFile` decodes with `ignoreBOM: true` and re-adds the BOM
+  itself.
+- **ripgrep exit status.** Since ripgrep 11.0.0, exit status 2 is returned
+  for any error, including soft errors such as an unreadable file, _even when
+  matches were found_
+  ([release notes](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases/tag/11.0.0)).
+  A grep tool that treats status 2 as "no results" therefore drops valid
+  matches.
+

+The PR review asked to make sure nothing that worked before breaks, that

+between the JavaScript and Rust versions. The three audits are in

+### 11.1 Compatibility options
+
+The JSON input format, the event types and the event envelope are unchanged.
+Old stored sessions still load: the storage schema was only widened. Each
+change that a script or a model could notice has an option that restores the
+previous behaviour. Every option is a CLI flag and a `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*`
+env var (`js/src/config/config.ts`, `COMPAT_DEFAULTS`).
+
+| Change                                                               | Option to restore the previous behaviour                      |
+| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| bash runs in `$SHELL` (if POSIX) or bash instead of `/bin/sh`        | `--bash-shell legacy` (or a shell path)                       |
+| bash keeps the tail of long output; edit/write return a confirmation | `--legacy-tool-output`                                        |
+| read past the end of a file is an error                              | `--legacy-tool-output`                                        |
+| edit rejects loose fuzzy matches and an empty `oldString` on a file  | `--legacy-edit-matching`                                      |
+| glob/ls do not follow symlinked directories                          | `--glob-follow-symlinks`                                      |
+| grep searches hidden files; grep times out after 30 s                | `--no-grep-hidden`, `--grep-timeout-ms 0`                     |
+| read returns at most 2000 lines / 50 KB                              | `--read-max-lines 0`, `--read-max-bytes 0`                    |
+| context overflow is `ContextOverflowError` in JSON output            | `--legacy-error-names` (reported as non-retryable `APIError`) |
+| `tokens.output` excludes reasoning tokens                            | `--legacy-token-usage`                                        |
+| a `stop` finish after tool calls continues the loop                  | `--legacy-loop-exit`                                          |
+| MCP connect is bounded (30 s)                                        | `--mcp-connect-timeout 0`, or `connect_timeout` per server    |
+
+MCP `timeout` keeps its previous meaning (listing tools). A first version of
+this PR also used it to bound connect, which broke slow servers configured
+with a short listing timeout, so connect got its own `connect_timeout`.

+### 11.2 Memory and resource leaks
+
+| #   | Leak (before)                                                                          | Fix                                                                                  |
+| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
+| 1   | SSE usage map grew by one entry per request                                            | Bounded to 64 entries, oldest evicted first                                          |
+| 2   | The usage tee branch stopped reading after 50 000 chars, so the tee buffered the rest  | Read to the end with a line tracker; only the unfinished line is kept                |
+| 3   | bash kept the whole output and was pinned by an abort listener on the turn signal      | Own `AbortController`, `capture: false`, bounded tail buffer                         |
+| 4   | grep buffered all rg output and stat-ed every match                                    | Streams rg output, one stat per file, stops after 10 000 matches                     |
+| 5   | FileTime read stamps stayed after a session was deleted                                | `FileTime.clear()` on `Session.remove`                                               |
+| 6   | Continuous/single-shot mode waited forever for `session.idle` if a prompt failed early | Wait for the prompt (or the HTTP request) to settle, then drop the idle subscription |
+| 7   | Retried 5xx/429 responses were dropped without cancelling the body                     | `response.body.cancel()` before retrying                                             |
+| 8   | Retry `sleep` left its abort listener on the turn signal                               | Listener removed when the delay elapses                                              |
+| 9   | `withTimeout` kept its timer when the promise rejected                                 | `finally(clearTimeout)`                                                              |
+| 10  | `Instance.dispose()` left the directory in the cache                                   | Removed from the cache                                                               |
+| 11  | Pending permission asks of a cancelled turn stayed until the instance was disposed     | `Permission.clearSession()` on cancel rejects them                                   |

+Left unchanged on purpose:
+
+- A client that disconnects from the HTTP server does not cancel the turn.
+  Clients that POST, disconnect and later poll the session rely on the turn
+  finishing.
+- The optional per-request provider timeout signal is not cleared early.
+  Clearing it would change the timeout semantics, and it holds no buffers.
+
+Tests: the leak regressions in `js/tests/compat-flags.ts`, plus
+`js/tests/sse-usage-extractor.ts`, `js/tests/bash-web-reliability.ts` and
+`js/tests/read-search-reliability-search.ts`.

+### 11.3 JavaScript and Rust parity
+
+The Rust port has the tools and the CLI, but no LLM, session, provider or
+MCP layer (that was so before this PR). For the tools, the audit
+([`js-rust-parity-audit.md`](../../../experiments/issue-335/audit/js-rust-parity-audit.md))
+compared every tool with the JS code as the reference, and the fixes are in
+[`rust-parity-fixes.md`](../../../experiments/issue-335/audit/rust-parity-fixes.md):
+
+- `grep`, `glob`, `list`, `read` and `edit` give the JS output, errors and
+  limits (the edit diff is the jsdiff format, checked against output of the
+  JS code); `bash` selects the shell like JS, closes stdin and kills the
+  process group; `todo` accepts the JS schema; `batch` reports every call
+  past the limit; `webfetch` and `websearch` match the JS messages and
+  parameters.
+- Latent bugs found on the way: a panic in `permission.rs` on non-ASCII
+  text before `&&`/`||`, a prefix match in `Filesystem::contains`
+  (`/a/bc` was "inside" `/a/b`), and a panic on an empty given id.
+- The same compatibility switches as in JS (`rust/src/compat.rs`): each is
+  a `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env var with a matching CLI flag, and each
+  legacy value restores what the previous Rust release did.
+  `--read-only` and `--disable-tools` were added for parity with JS.
+
+Left as they are, with reasons:
+
+- No FileTime and no per-file lock in Rust: each CLI run is a separate
+  process without a session, and `batch` runs calls one after another, so
+  a lock is never contended and a read stamp cannot outlive the process.
+- `permission.rs` is not consulted by the tools, because the Rust CLI never
+  runs tools for a model.
+- Small output differences listed under "Deliberate divergences" in
+  `rust-parity-fixes.md` (bash default timeout 2 min vs 1 min, stdout and
+  stderr joined with a separator, the markdown converter).

+export async function withLock<T>(filepath: string, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
+  const current = state()
+  const currentLock = current.locks.get(filepath) ?? Promise.resolve()
+  let release: () => void = () => {}
+  const nextLock = new Promise<void>((resolve) => { release = resolve })

+## 3. FileTime check breaks on future mtimes and unnormalized paths (MEDIUM)

+- **Upstream:**

+- **Bug A, future mtime:**

+  - `assert` compares `stats.mtime > readTime(new Date())`, so the file can **never** be edited, even immediately after a read.
+  - Fast writers with coarse mtime resolution can also slip past the check: an external write landing within the same timestamp tick is not detected.
+- **Bug B, path normalization:**
+  - `read` resolves the path one way, for example `dir/a.txt`, and `edit` gets `dir/./a.txt`, `dir/x/../a.txt` or a trailing-slash variant.
+  - The result is "You must read the file … before overwriting it".

+- **Proof:** `experiments-A/03-filetime-future-mtime.ts`:
+  - mtime +60s, then read, then edit, fails with "has been modified since it was last read".
+  - Read `dir/a.txt` then edit `dir/./a.txt` fails with "You must read the file…".
+- **Verdict: PORT.**
+

+- **In `time.ts`:**

+## 1. CRITICAL: glob and ls hang forever when there are more than about 15k files. PORT (JS)

+- **Upstream:** e5b33f8a5e (#10833, 2026-01-29) passes an `AbortSignal` into `Ripgrep.files`. +- **Bug:** `glob.ts:32-34` and `ls.ts:63` `break` after 100 results. The generator's `finally` in `file/ripgrep.ts:273-276` then runs this:
+  ```ts
+  } finally {
+    reader.releaseLock();
+    await proc.exited;
+  }
+  ```
+  Nobody reads stdout any more, so rg blocks writing into the full pipe and `proc.exited` never resolves. +- **Proof** (`e2-files-early-break.ts`, using a copy of `files()`): with 10k files it collects 100 in 43 ms. +- **Fix** (plain code, no Effect) in `file/ripgrep.ts`:
+  ```ts
+  export async function* files(input: { cwd: string; glob?: string[]; signal?: AbortSignal }) {
+    input.signal?.throwIfAborted();
+    ...
+    const proc = Bun.spawn(args, { cwd: input.cwd, stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'ignore',
+                                   maxBuffer: 1024 * 1024 * 20, signal: input.signal });
+    ...
+    try {
+      while (true) { input.signal?.throwIfAborted(); const { done, value } = await reader.read(); ... }
+      if (buffer) yield buffer;
+    } finally {
+      await reader.cancel().catch(() => {});
+      if (proc.exitCode === null) proc.kill();
+      await proc.exited;
+    }
+    input.signal?.throwIfAborted();
+  }
+  ```

+### 1. [HIGH, security] In plan/readonly mode the bash permission scan ignores output redirects, so `echo x > file` writes files
+
+- **Upstream:** e7ff7143b6, PR #6737, 2026-01-30, "handle redirected_statement treesitter node in bash permissions".
+  - Upstream fix: the permission pattern becomes `node.parent?.type === "redirected_statement" ? node.parent.text : node.text`, so the redirect is part of the text that is matched.
+  - Upstream has no readonly mode, so with `echo*` it would still allow the command. **Our version needs a stronger, adapted fix.**
+- **Our bug:**
+  - js/src/tool/bash.ts:104-122 builds tokens only from `command` children of type command_name/word/string/raw_string/concatenation. A `file_redirect` is a sibling under `redirected_statement`, so it is dropped.
+  - `echo hi > x.txt` therefore yields `['echo','hi']`, which matches `'echo*': 'allow'` (js/src/permission/index.ts:69, readonlyBash).
+  - Our own string evaluator already guards this case (js/src/permission/index.ts:219-225, `hasRedirection = />>?/`), but the bash tool calls `checkBashTokens` (index.ts:520-560), not `evaluateBash`.
+- **Proof:** experiments-C/bash-redirect-readonly.ts, run with permissionMode=readonly:
+  ```
+  string evaluator (evaluateBash) on same command: deny
+  BLOCKED : rm -f nothing
+  ALLOWED : echo pwned > written.txt
+  ALLOWED : cat /etc/hostname >> appended.txt
+  files written in readonly mode: [ "written.txt", "appended.txt" ]
+  ```
+- **Logic to apply** (adapted; verified in experiments-C/redirect-detect.ts):
+  ```ts
+  const WRITE_OPS = new Set(['>', '>>', '>|', '&>', '&>>', '>&']);
+  function writeRedirects(root): string[] {
+    const hits = [];
+    for (const r of root.descendantsOfType('file_redirect')) {
+      if (!r) continue;
+      let op = '';
+      for (let i = 0; i < r.childCount; i++) { const c = r.child(i); if (c && WRITE_OPS.has(c.type)) op = c.type; }
+      const dest = r.childForFieldName('destination')?.text ?? r.lastChild?.text ?? '';
+      if (!op || dest === '/dev/null') continue;
+      if (op === '>&' && /^\d+$|^-$/.test(dest)) continue;   // 2>&1
+      hits.push(r.text);
+    }
+    return hits;
+  }
+  ```
+  Results from the experiment:
+
+  | Command | Flagged? |
+  |---|---|
+  | `> x.txt`, `>> b`, `{ echo a; } > f`, `&> log`, `>| f` | yes |
+  | `2>/dev/null`, `2>&1`, `< in.txt`, heredoc | no |
+- **How to apply:**
+  - In bash.ts, right after the tree is built (l.99-102), call `writeRedirects(tree.rootNode)`.
+  - If it returns anything, make it resolve to the policy's catch-all action. For example, push one extra entry into `commands` that only `'*'` matches, such as `['>', ...hits]`.
+  - Alternatively, add a `redirects: string[]` input to `checkBashTokens` that is evaluated as `patterns['*']`, raising a deny or adding an ask pattern.
+- **Failing test:** set `config.permissionMode = 'readonly'` and run BashTool with `echo pwned > f.txt`. Expect a rejection and no f.txt. Today it is allowed and the file is created.
+- **Rust:** rust/src/tool/bash.rs has no permission scan. N/A.

+### 3. [HIGH] Bash output: unbounded memory, O(n^2) metadata, head truncation drops the error tail, and split UTF-8
+
+- **Upstream:**
+  - 307251bf3c, PR #22660, 2026-04-15, "bash memory usage".
+  - 754ea99d86, PR #39403, 2026-07-28, "preserve shell output tail".
+  - 2092350cfa, PR #41007, 2026-08-07, "align shell output limits".
+  - Streaming text decode: the snapshot shell.ts uses `Stream.decodeText`.
+- **Our bugs:**
+  - bash.ts:185 `output += chunk.data.toString()`: the whole output is kept in memory, and the full string is sent to `ctx.metadata` on every chunk (l.186-191). Each call is a `Session.updatePart` storage write plus a Bus publish.
+  - bash.ts:214-216 `output.slice(0, MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH)` keeps the head and drops the tail, which is where compiler and test errors appear.
+  - bash.ts:185 also decodes each Buffer chunk on its own, so a multi-byte character split across chunks becomes two U+FFFD.
+- **Proof** (experiments-C/bash-behaviour.ts and bash-utf8-split.ts):
+  - (2) For 100 KB of output ending in FINAL-ERROR-LINE: `tail kept? false head kept? true`.
+  - (3) For 4 MB of output: 47 metadata calls carrying 71,489,792 chars in total, with RSS +21.7 MB. The tool output itself is only 30 KB.
+  - bash-utf8-split.ts: 3 euro signs split across chunks gave `intact: 0 replacement chars: 6`.
+- **Upstream logic** (from /tmp/upstream/last/packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts:220-253 and 436-500, Effect and truncation-file stripped):
+  ```ts
+  const MAX_METADATA_LENGTH = 30_000;
+  function preview(text: string) {
+    if (text.length <= MAX_METADATA_LENGTH) return text;
+    return '...\n\n' + text.slice(-MAX_METADATA_LENGTH);
+  }
+  function tail(text: string, maxLines: number, maxBytes: number) {
+    const lines = text.split('\n');
+    if (lines.length <= maxLines && Buffer.byteLength(text, 'utf-8') <= maxBytes) return { text, cut: false };
+    const out: string[] = []; let bytes = 0;
+    for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0 && out.length < maxLines; i--) {
+      const size = Buffer.byteLength(lines[i], 'utf-8') + (out.length > 0 ? 1 : 0);
+      if (bytes + size > maxBytes) {
+        if (out.length === 0) {
+          const buf = Buffer.from(lines[i], 'utf-8');
+          let start = Math.max(0, buf.length - maxBytes);
+          while (start < buf.length && (buf[start] & 0xc0) === 0x80) start++;
+          out.unshift(buf.subarray(start).toString('utf-8'));
+        }
+        break;
+      }
+      out.unshift(lines[i]); bytes += size;
+    }
+    return { text: out.join('\n'), cut: true };
+  }
+  // streaming loop
+  const keep = MAX_BYTES * 2; const list: { text: string; size: number }[] = [];
+  let used = 0, cut = false, last = '';
+  const decoder = new TextDecoder();
+  for await (const chunk of command.stream()) {
+    if (chunk.type === 'exit') { exit = chunk.code; continue; }
+    const text = decoder.decode(chunk.data, { stream: true });
+    const size = Buffer.byteLength(text, 'utf-8');
+    list.push({ text, size }); used += size;
+    while (used > keep && list.length > 1) { used -= list.shift()!.size; cut = true; }
+    last = preview(last + text);
+    ctx.metadata({ metadata: { output: last, description: params.description } });
+  }
+  const end = tail(list.map((i) => i.text).join(''), MAX_LINES, MAX_BYTES);
+  output = (cut || end.cut ? '...output truncated...\n\n' : '') + end.text;
+  ```
+- **How to apply:**
+  - Replace bash.ts:135 and :181-193 with the loop above.
+  - Replace bash.ts:214-217 with the `tail()` result. Use MAX_BYTES = 30_000, which keeps the current documented limit; upstream uses 50 KB and 2000 lines.
+  - Keep the timeout and abort notices appended after the output (l.219-225). Metadata `output` at l.247 should be `last`.
+  - Optionally throttle `ctx.metadata`, for example once every 100 ms. Upstream does not do this, but each call is a full storage write.
+  - Update bash.txt:23 to "the beginning of the output is dropped".
+- **Failing tests:**
+  - (a) `printf start; head -c 100000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' x; echo FINAL; exit 3`: expect the output to contain `FINAL`.
+  - (b) Record every `ctx.metadata` payload: expect each payload to be at most 30_006 chars.
+  - (c) `printf '\342\202'; sleep 0.2; printf '\254'`: expect `€`.
+- **Rust:** bash.rs:125-127 needs the same tail-keeping truncation. It also has a **crash** at that spot:
+  - `output.truncate(MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH)` panics when byte 30000 is not on a char boundary.
+  - Proof: experiments-C/rust/truncate_panic.rs → `assertion failed: self.is_char_boundary(new_len)`.
+  - Fix: port `tail()` with the same UTF-8 continuation-byte skip, or truncate at `floor_char_boundary`.

+### 5. [MEDIUM] webfetch timeout: the timer leaks when fetch rejects, and the body read is not covered
+
+- **Upstream:**
+  - bc1840b196, PR #21378, 2026-04-07: try/finally clears the timer.
+  - The upstream core version (69f1ec22e3, PR #33259, 2026-06-21) runs the body read under the request timeout.
+- **Our bugs:**
+  - js/src/tool/webfetch.ts:53-54 arms the timer, and l.76-86 runs `await verboseFetch(...)` and then `clearTimeout`. If the fetch rejects (DNS failure, ECONNREFUSED, TLS), the timer stays pending for up to 120 s and keeps a one-shot CLI process alive.
+  - The timer is also cleared before `arrayBuffer()` (l.98), so a server that sends headers and then trickles the body is never timed out.
+- **Proof:**
+  - experiments-C/webfetch-timer-leak.ts: `fetch failed after ms 8` but `process exit after ms 8007`.
+  - experiments-C/webfetch-behaviour.ts (4): with `timeout: 1` and a body trickling for 3 s, it returned success after `ms: 3280`.
+- **Upstream logic:**
+  ```ts
+  const response = await (async () => {
+    try { return await fetch(url, { signal, headers }); }
+    finally { clearTimeout(timeoutId); }
+  })();
+  ```
+- **How to apply:**
+  - Clear the timer in a `finally` that wraps both the fetch **and** the body read (l.76-101), not right after headers arrive.
+  - Simplest is `const signal = AbortSignal.any([AbortSignal.timeout(timeout), ctx.abort])` with no manual timer at all. `AbortSignal.timeout` does not keep the process alive, and its abort also cancels the body stream.
+- **Failing tests:**
+  - (a) Fetch `http://127.0.0.1:9/` with timeout 8 in a child process: expect the process to exit in under 1 s.
+  - (b) A local server that trickles the body for 3 s, with `timeout: 1`: expect a "timed out" error.
+- **websearch.ts:89-114 and codesearch.ts:71-96** use the same pattern, but they clear the timer in both try and catch, so there is no leak. The body read (`response.text()`, websearch.ts:114, codesearch.ts:96) is still outside the timeout. Apply the same `AbortSignal.timeout` change there.
+- **Rust:** reqwest's `ClientBuilder::timeout` (webfetch.rs:107) covers the body and has no timer to leak. N/A.

+### 7. [MEDIUM] web tool bodies are buffered without a bound
+
+- **Upstream:** 69f1ec22e3, PR #33259, 2026-06-21, "bound web tool failures". It adds `collectBoundedResponseBody` (packages/core/src/tool/http-body.ts), used by webfetch and websearch. The same commit also maps a converter throw to an error result.
+- **Our bug:**
+  - webfetch.ts:93-101 checks `content-length` and then `await response.arrayBuffer()`, so a chunked or lying response is buffered in full before the 5 MB check.
+  - websearch.ts:114 and codesearch.ts:96 call `response.text()` with no cap at all.
+- **Proof:** experiments-C/webfetch-behaviour.ts (5): a 20 MB chunked body gave `Response too large`, but the server had sent all `20` MB first. An endless body would grow until OOM.
+- **Upstream logic** (Effect stripped):
+  ```ts
+  async function readBounded(res: Response, max: number, tooLarge: () => Error) {
+    const n = Number.parseInt(res.headers.get('content-length') ?? '', 10);
+    if (Number.isSafeInteger(n) && n > max) throw tooLarge();
+    const chunks: Uint8Array[] = []; let size = 0;
+    const reader = res.body!.getReader();
+    for (;;) {
+      const { done, value } = await reader.read();
+      if (done) break;
+      size += value.byteLength;
+      if (size > max) { await reader.cancel(); throw tooLarge(); }
+      chunks.push(value);
+    }
+    return Buffer.concat(chunks, size);
+  }
+  ```
+- **How to apply:**
+  - Replace webfetch.ts:93-101 with `const arrayBuffer = await readBounded(response, MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE, () => new Error('Response too large (exceeds 5MB limit)'))`.
+  - In websearch/codesearch, use `readBounded(response, 5MB, ...)` and then `.toString('utf8')`.
+- **Failing test:** a server streams 20 x 1 MB chunks with no content-length. Expect an error after at most 6 chunks have been pulled; today all 20 are pulled.
+- **Rust:** webfetch.rs:150-153 `response.bytes().await` has the same problem. Use `response.chunk()` in a loop with a cap. websearch.rs:186 and codesearch.rs have the same issue.

+### 2. Provider stream-error objects are misclassified, so retryable 5xx are never retried — HIGH (our own bug, exposed by upstream `62f38087b8` #12768 and `027d43b5ea` 2025-12-01)
+
+**Bug.** With AI SDK 7, a mid-stream provider error reaches `processor.ts:273-290` as a plain object built by `createProviderStreamError`. It looks like `{ message, type, code, statusCode, isRetryable, data }`.
+- OpenAI and Anthropic set `code` to a STRING (`'server_error'`, `'overloaded_error'`, `'insufficient_quota'`, ...) and `statusCode` to a NUMBER.
+
+**Ours** (`message-v2.ts:872-886`):
+
+```ts
+const rawCode = candidate['code'] ?? candidate['statusCode'] ?? candidate['status'] ?? root['code'] ?? root['statusCode'] ?? root['status'];
+const statusCode = typeof rawCode === 'number' ? rawCode : typeof rawCode === 'string' && /^\d+$/.test(rawCode) ? ... : undefined;
+if (statusCode === undefined) return;
+```
+
+The string `code` wins the `??` chain and then fails the digit test, so the function returns `undefined`.
+- The error becomes `NamedError.Unknown`, and the `isRetryableAPIError` check (processor.ts:615) is false.
+- The result: Anthropic `overloaded_error` (529) and OpenAI `server_error` (500) / `server_is_overloaded` (503) end the session instead of backing off.
+- The SDK's own `isRetryable` is also ignored. :907 recomputes it from the status alone, so `insufficient_quota` (429) is retried for the full 7-day budget.
+
+**Upstream logic** (`provider/error.ts parseStreamError`, plus the SDK fields):
+
+```ts
+const code = typeof err.code === "string" ? err.code : undefined
+if (code === "context_length_exceeded") return overflow
+if (code === "insufficient_quota" || code === "usage_not_included" || code === "invalid_prompt") return APIError({ isRetryable: false, ... })
+if (code === "server_is_overloaded" || code === "server_error") return APIError({ isRetryable: true, ... })
+```
+
+**Apply** in `normalizeProviderErrorObject`:
+- Take the numeric status first: `const num = [candidate.statusCode, candidate.status, root.statusCode, root.status, candidate.code, root.code].find(v => typeof v === 'number' || (typeof v === 'string' && /^\d+$/.test(v)))`.
+- Keep `const strCode = [candidate.code, root.code, candidate.type, root.type].find(v => typeof v === 'string' && !/^\d+$/.test(v))`.
+- Return when both are absent. Classify `context_length_exceeded` as overflow (#1).
+- Set `isRetryable` as follows:
+  - `false` for the three quota/prompt codes above;
+  - `true` for `server_error`, `server_is_overloaded`, `overloaded_error`, `api_error`, `rate_limit_error`;
+  - otherwise `typeof root.isRetryable === 'boolean' ? root.isRetryable : status===429 || status>=500`.

+**Failing tests:**
+- `fromError({ message:'The server had an error', type:'server_error', code:'server_error', statusCode:500, isRetryable:true }, {providerID:'openai'})` should give `name==='APIError'` with `data.isRetryable===true`. Today it is `UnknownError`.

+- `{ code:'insufficient_quota', statusCode:429, isRetryable:false }` should have `isRetryable===false`.

Fixes #53149
Fixes #53151
Refs #45927

> [!NOTE]
> Not ready to merge yet. Eval results are below.

## Problem

The edit tool picked one line ending for the whole file: `source.includes("\r\n") ? "\r\n" : "\n"`. If a file contained a single CRLF, every `\n` in both `oldString` and `newString` was rewritten to CRLF. In mixed-ending files this:

- wrote CRLF into regions that used LF (one CRLF in the file became two after an edit), and
- made multi-line `oldString` values fail with the misleading "must match exactly, including whitespace and indentation" error.

The read tool strips `\r`, so the model never sees CRLF and had no way to work around it.

## Fix

- Matching (exact, then Unicode-normalized, then trailing-whitespace) runs against an LF view of the source, which is the same text the read tool shows. Match offsets are mapped back to source offsets, so untouched bytes keep their original endings.
- Inside a match, replacement lines are aligned with the matched lines (longest common subsequence). A line that is kept or changed in place reuses the ending of its source line, so unchanged context keeps its bytes even in a mixed-ending file. Only added lines take the dominant ending of the matched region, or the file's dominant ending for a single-line match or a tie.
- If `oldString` and `newString` differ only in `\r`, the edit is treated as a line-ending change and applied to the exact bytes. Explicit CRLF↔LF conversion still works.
- An edit that would leave the file unchanged now fails instead of reporting success (#45927). The error says how to change line endings explicitly.
- The tool description now says to write line breaks as `\n`, that existing endings are preserved, how to change endings explicitly, and the lenient fallback tiers that were previously undocumented.

## Testing

- Unit tests cover the byte-level repro from #53149 (`head\r\nAAA OLD BBB\ntail\n`), a mostly-CRLF file whose `oldString` crosses a lone LF line, unchanged context inside a mixed-ending match, explicit CRLF→LF conversion, and the no-op failure.
- `bun test test/tool-edit.test.ts` in `packages/core`: 20 pass.
- `bun run check`: passes.

## Eval results

The runs come from two [dumber](https://github.com/anomalyco/evals/tree/main/dumber) evals: [`line-endings`](https://github.com/anomalyco/evals/blob/main/dumber/evals/line-endings/eval.ts) and [`line-endings-realistic`](https://github.com/anomalyco/evals/blob/main/dumber/evals/line-endings-realistic/eval.ts). 20 models (DeepSeek, Grok, Muse, Gemini, GLM, MiniMax, Claude, Kimi, Qwen; GPT is left out because it gets `patch` instead of `edit`) × cases × 3 repetitions. Trials only get `read`, `glob`, `grep` and `edit`, so every byte on disk went through the edit tool. Baseline is `0bef0ea` (`v2`), v1 is `64eb0f6` (this PR's first commit), v2 is `d38a53b` (this PR's current head). The variants ran at the same time. The baseline and v1 were each run twice to measure noise.

### `line-endings-realistic`: multi-file feature work in a mixed C#/TS/Python/Rust repo (360 trials per run)

The repo has CRLF, LF and mixed-ending files. No prompt mentions line endings. Pass = every requested change is present and no line ending was damaged.

| | baseline | v1 | **v2** |
|---|---|---|---|
| pass rate | 32.5% / 30.8% | 82.8% / 80.8% | **98.3%** |
| trials with clean line endings | 120 / 116 | 303 / 292 | **359 / 359** |
| damaged line endings, total | 1380 / 1331 | 154 / 192 | **0** |
| failed edit calls | 445 / 547 | 278 / 290 | 255 |
| mean trial time | 87.5s / 89.1s | 76.8s / 73.7s | **71.0s** |
| tokens | 142M / 154M | 120M / 133M | **107M** |
| cost | $57.4 / $58.5 | $51.0 / $51.8 | **$48.5** |

Pass rate per case (out of 60):

| case | baseline | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| add-discount | 0, 0 | 60, 60 | 60 |
| category-two-turns | 0, 0 | 54, 54 | 59 |
| add-delete | 1, 1 | 45, 47 | 59 |
| rename-sku | 16, 19 | 14, 19 | 56 |
| move-item-value | 34, 39 | 59, 60 | 60 |
| seed-and-docs | 60, 58 | 59, 58 | 60 |

v1 still damaged line endings: unchanged context inside a multi-line match took the region's dominant ending. v2's per-line alignment removes all of it. The remaining v2 failures are missing requirements (model mistakes) plus one Gemini `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL`, not line endings. Fewer failed edits also mean fewer retries, which is where the drops in time (about −20%), tokens (about −28%) and cost (about −16%) come from.

### `line-endings`: single-file edits with known bytes (780 trials per run)

| | baseline | v1 | **v2** |
|---|---|---|---|
| pass rate | 90.0% / 90.0% | 94.1% / 93.3% | **96.2%** |
| `mixed-single-crlf` (#53149) | 19/60, 20/60 | 60/60, 57/60 | **60/60** |
| `crlf-convert-to-lf` | 30/60, 23/60 | 15/60, 11/60 | 33/60 |
| tool reported success, file unchanged | 12 / 14 | 19 / 28 | 9 |
| mean trial time, excluding conversion | 16.7s / 16.1s | 12.6s / 13.2s | 13.7s |

11 of the 13 cases are at or near 100% in every variant.

- v1 regressed explicit conversion. Because every `\n` was normalized, `crlf-convert-to-lf` could no longer be done with `edit`, and the tool reported success on a no-op. v2 fixes both. The 9 remaining "unchanged" trials are models that changed the file and then reverted it themselves; the tool now rejects true no-ops.
- Known gap: `crlf-convert-to-lf` with only `edit` still passes about half the time, and about a third of trials hit the 300s timeout. Many models (Claude included) write `\r` as a literal backslash escape instead of a real carriage return, so their `oldString` never matches. With a shell available this case is trivial.

### Full tool set (shell, write, subagents, …)

Same evals with OpenCode's full tool set, baseline `0bef0ea` vs v2 `d38a53b`, run at the same time. The `LINE_ENDINGS_TOOLS=all` switch and the raw runs are in [anomalyco/evals#15](https://github.com/anomalyco/evals/pull/15).

| | baseline | **v2** |
|---|---|---|
| `line-endings-realistic` pass rate | 34.2% | **91.7%** |
| trials with clean line endings | 132 / 358 | **343 / 360** |
| `line-endings` pass rate | 95.8% | **99.5%** |
| `mixed-single-crlf` | 36/60 | **60/60** |
| `line-endings` mean trial time / tokens / cost | 17.3s / 28.5M / $18.9 | **15.1s / 23.1M / $15.7** |
| `line-endings-realistic` mean trial time / tokens / cost | 91.4s / 186M / $66.1 | 100.9s / 185M / $64.9 |

Realistic pass rate per case (out of 60): add-delete 5 → 55, add-discount 4 → 56, category-two-turns 2 → 52, move-item-value 44 → 60, rename-sku 11 → 47, seed-and-docs 57 → 60.

None of the 17 damaged v2 realistic trials was damaged by `edit`:

- 12 used `write` to rewrite a whole CRLF file with LF (DeepSeek V4 Pro accounts for 11 of them, MiniMax M3 for 1). The same trials are damaged on the baseline too.
- 5 rewrote a file with a Python one-liner through `shell` (text-mode read/write turns CRLF into LF).
- 2 are Claude Opus deliberately normalizing a mixed-ending `.cs` file to CRLF with `perl`, as `.gitattributes` asks. The scorer counts that as damage, but it is a reasonable choice.

The realistic time difference comes from provider stalls that hit the 600s timeout: MiniMax M3 and Gemini 3.8 Flash account for 9 timeouts vs 7 on the baseline, with idle sessions and almost no edits. Median trial time is 52s vs 50s, and tokens and cost are flat.

### Not covered yet

- `write` does not preserve line endings when it overwrites an existing file. It is now the main remaining source of damage with the full tool set. A follow-up could keep the overwritten file's ending.
- `patch` (used for GPT models) does not touch line endings and is not covered by these evals.
- With only `edit`, explicit CRLF→LF conversion still fails about half the time because models write `\r` as a literal escape.

+# JS ↔ Rust parity audit (issue #335 branch)
+
+Scope: `js/src` (primary, Bun/TS) vs `rust/src` (tools + CLI only). This is a read-only audit; no source files were changed.
+
+Branch column: **B** means the divergence was introduced or touched by this branch (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`). **U** means it was unchanged by the branch, so it pre-dates it.
+
+Files changed by the branch:
+- JS: `ripgrep.ts`, `time.ts`, `bash.ts/.txt`, `codesearch.ts`, `edit.ts`, `glob.ts`, `grep.ts`, `ls.ts`, `read.ts`, `task.ts`, `tool.ts`, `webfetch.ts/.txt`, `websearch.ts/.txt`, `write.ts`, and the new `util/bom.ts`, `util/exa-mcp.ts`, `util/read-bounded.ts`.
+- Rust: `bash.rs`, `codesearch.rs`, `edit.rs`, `glob.rs`, `grep.rs`, `read.rs`, `webfetch.rs`, `websearch.rs`, `write.rs`, plus tests.
+
+Files not touched by the branch:
+- Rust: `list.rs`, `batch.rs`, `todo.rs`, `invalid.rs`, `multiedit.rs`, `util/*`, `id.rs`, `permission.rs`, `cli.rs`.
+- JS: `batch.ts`, `todo.ts`, `invalid.ts`, `registry.ts`, `permission/index.ts`, `id.ts`, `binary.ts`, `filesystem.ts`.
+
+## 0. Cross-cutting
+
+| # | Divergence | JS | Rust | Br |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| X1 | **Raw args vs defaults.** JS validates with zod but passes the raw args to `execute`, so defaults and coercions are not applied. Rust serde applies `#[serde(default)]`, and its typed ints reject strings, negatives and floats that JS normalises (read/bash/webfetch). | `tool/tool.ts` L95-110 | each `*Params` struct | U |
+| X2 | **Error wrapper text.** JS validation error: "The X tool was called with invalid arguments: …\nPlease rewrite the input…". Rust uses the `AgentError` Display: "Invalid arguments for tool 'x': …", "Tool execution failed: …", "File not found: p". Rust suggestions appear only in `to_json`. | `tool/tool.ts` L95-110 | `error.rs`, `tool/mod.rs` | U |
+| X3 | **Path resolution.** JS calls `path.resolve(Instance.directory, p)`, which normalises `..`, and builds titles with `relative(Instance.worktree, …)`. Rust calls `working_directory.join(p)` with no normalisation, and `relative_path` strips the cwd prefix or returns the absolute path. | per-tool | `tool/context.rs` L63-77 | U |
+| X4 | **Registry.** JS registers `task` and does not register `multiedit`; Rust is the reverse. JS also filters `deniedTools` (READ_ONLY_DENIED_TOOLS + config.disableTools); Rust has no equivalent. | `tool/registry.ts` L28-55, L76-93 | `tool/mod.rs` L87-104 | U |
+| X5 | **Permissions.** JS tools call `Permission.check`/`ask` (edit, write, bash, webfetch). Rust ports the policy faithfully in `permission.rs`, but **no Rust tool calls it**; only `cli.rs` validates it. | `permission/index.ts` | `permission.rs`; `cli.rs` L243-250, L381 | U |
+| X6 | **FileTime.** JS records reads, asserts read-before-edit/write, and serialises edits with a per-file lock. Rust has none of this. | `file/time.ts`; read.ts L246; edit.ts L83, L106; write.ts L30-53 | — | B (JS side touched) |
+| X7 | **BOM.** Bun `file.text()` and `Bom.split/join` strip and restore a UTF-8 BOM. Rust `read_to_string` keeps U+FEFF in the content. | `util/bom.ts`; edit.ts L107, L121-126 | read.rs, edit.rs | B |
+
+## 1. Tools
+
+### read (`js/src/tool/read.ts` ↔ `rust/src/tool/read.rs`)
+| Divergence | JS | Rust | Br |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **Empty file.** JS returns 1 line ("total 1 lines"); Rust returns 0 lines ("total 0 lines"). The line splitters differ: JS uses `/\r?\n/` and pops a trailing `''`, Rust uses `lines()`. | L261-265 | L177 | B |
+| **BOM.** JS strips it; Rust shows U+FEFF on line 1. | Bun text() | L~170 | B |
+| **Numeric params.** JS accepts offset/limit given as strings, negatives or floats; Rust's `usize` rejects them. | L23-38, L292-298 | params | B |
+| **Images.** Rust always validates, with no `supportsImages` check and no `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_VERIFY_IMAGES_AT_READ_TOOL` toggle. Its error text is shorter and it takes the mime type from a fixed table. | L~300-390 | L403-459 | U |
+| **canonical_name.** Rust does not apply NFC normalisation. | L271-276 | L346-354 | B |
+| **Not found.** Rust does not put the suggestions in the message text. | | | U |
+| **Mid-character offset.** `byte_offset_to_char_index` differs when the offset falls inside a multibyte character. | | text_window | B |

+| **WhitespaceNormalized / EscapeNormalized.** The algorithms differ; Rust lacks the `\\\n` case. | L389-437 | L427-466 | U |

+### multiedit
+| Divergence | JS | Rust | Br |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Registered in Rust only. With `edits: []`, JS throws a TypeError (`results.at(-1)!`) while Rust returns empty output. | `multiedit.ts` L52 | `multiedit.rs` L111 | U |
+
+### write
+| Divergence | JS | Rust | Br |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **Missing in Rust.** No permission, no lock, no `FileTime.read` after the write. | L30-53 | `write.rs` | B(JS) |
+| **write.txt claim.** It says "MUST use the Read tool first", but JS does not enforce this for write. | `write.txt` | — | U |
+
+### bash (`js/src/tool/bash.ts` ↔ `rust/src/tool/bash.rs`)
+| Divergence | JS | Rust | Br |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **Default timeout.** JS 60 000 ms; Rust 120 000 ms. | L21 | L18 | B |
+| **Shell.** JS `selectShell` uses `$SHELL` (excluding fish and nu) and falls back to bash/sh. Rust always runs `bash -c`. | L47-63 | L111 | B |
+| **stdin.** JS uses `'ignore'`; Rust inherits stdin, so a command that reads stdin hangs. | L301 | L111-ish | B |
+| **Output.** JS interleaves stdout and stderr in arrival order. Rust prints stdout, then `"\n--- stderr ---\n"`, then stderr. | L236-260 | L253-268 | B |
+| **Title.** JS uses the command; Rust uses the description or the first 3 words. | L377 | L98-106 | U |
+| **Metadata.** JS: `{output, exit, signal, timedOut, aborted, description}`. Rust: `{exitCode, exit, signal, output, command, [timedOut]}`. | L370-390 | L160-175 | B |
+| **Timeout text.** JS: "(Command timed out after N ms)" plus "Exit code unavailable (signal SIGTERM)". Rust: "Command timed out after Nms". | `process-result.ts` | L147-157 | B |
+| **Kill and abort.** JS kills the process tree with SIGTERM→SIGKILL and supports abort. Rust sends SIGKILL to the child only and has no abort. | | | B |
+| **Validation.** JS rejects a negative timeout; Rust's `u64` rejects floats and strings. | L174-178 | params | B |
+| **Permissions.** JS runs a tree-sitter permission scan of the command; Rust has none. | L187-229 | — | U |
+| **Description.** Rust still says "persistent shell session". | | description | U |

+### glob (`js/src/tool/glob.ts` + `file/ripgrep.ts` ↔ `rust/src/tool/glob.rs`)
+| Divergence | JS | Rust | Br |
+|---|---|---|---|

+| **Symlinks.** JS (rg without `--follow`) does not follow them; Rust (glob crate metadata) does. | | | U |
+| **.git.** JS excludes it; Rust does not, so `**/*` lists `.git/**`. | | | U |

+# Memory and resource leak audit (issue #335)
+
+Scope: `js/src` (primary, long-running CLI / continuous / server modes) and
+`rust/src` (tools + CLI). Read-only audit; no source file was edited.
+Bun 1.4.4. Every finding below was checked against the surrounding code.
+
+Severity: high = grows per tool call / LLM step in normal use; medium = per
+session or per turn; low = bounded or one-off.
+
+Experiments (all in this directory; run from `js/` with
+`timeout 90 bun ../experiments/issue-335/audit/<file>.ts`):
+
+| Script | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| `sse-usage-growth.ts` | 1000 simulated steps -> 1000 retained entries; one `consumeLatestUsage()` removes 1 (999 left). CONFIRMED |
+| `tee-no-cancel.ts` | 25 MB streamed response: peak extra RSS 25 MB when the usage branch only `break`s, 7 MB when it also cancels. CONFIRMED |
+| `abort-any-retention.ts` | `AbortSignal.any([longLived, ...])` + abort listener: 0/200 listener closures collected while the parent lives (200/200 without a listener, 200/200 once the timeout source fires). CONFIRMED |
+

+
+## Confirmed
+
+### 1. `SSEUsageExtractor.pendingUsage` grows by one entry per LLM request (high)
+
+- Where: `js/src/util/sse-usage-extractor.ts:15` (`const pendingUsage = new Map()`).
+  Entries are added in `processStreamForUsage` (`:86`). The callers are
+  `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1212` (non-verbose path) and `:1390` (verbose path).
+- Resource: one `SSEUsageData` per streamed response that carries a usage
+  chunk. Small entries, but a module-level map that is never pruned.
+- Growth trigger: every LLM step whose SSE body carries usage. The only consumer
+  is `js/src/session/processor.ts:483` (`consumeLatestUsage()`). It runs only
+  when the AI SDK reported zero tokens, so with a normal provider nothing is
+  ever removed. Even when it does run, it removes only the newest entry.
+- Side effect (correctness): when the SDK does report 0 tokens,
+  `consumeLatestUsage` picks the newest entry across all sessions and requests.
+  With concurrent sessions in server mode, it can pick up another request's
+  usage.
+- Fix: return the request id with the response (or keep a per-request
+  callback) and `consumeUsage(id)` at finish-step. Minimal option: keep only
+  the latest entry (`pendingUsage.clear()` before `set`), or cap the map to the
+  last ~16 entries.
+
+### 2. Usage tee branch is abandoned without `cancel()` (medium: per-response duplication, released at stream end)
+
+- Where: `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1199-1216` (non-verbose path, the default).
+  ```ts
+  const [sdkStream, usageStream] = response.body.tee();
+  ... if (body.length > 50000) break;   // reader never cancelled
+  ```
+- Resource: the tee keeps queueing every later chunk into the unread
+  `usageStream` branch until the response ends. Peak memory for every LLM
+  response over 50 KB is therefore 2x the response size; the experiment
+  measured 25 MB extra for a 25 MB stream versus 7 MB with cancel.
+- Second effect: a tee source is cancelled only when *both* branches cancel.
+  If the SDK cancels its branch without aborting the fetch (for example it
+  stops consuming early), the HTTP body keeps downloading into the orphaned
+  branch.
+- Functional bug in the same spot: usage is normally in the last SSE chunk.
+  Cutting at the first 50 KB means long responses never yield usage, so the
+  #249 fallback silently fails for them.
+- Fix: after the loop, call `reader.cancel().catch(() => {})`. Do not
+  `await` it inline: by the Streams spec a tee branch's cancel promise settles
+  only when the other branch also cancels or the source closes. The first
+  version of the experiment deadlocked on exactly this. Better still, keep
+  reading to the end but retain only a rolling tail (for example the last 8 KB)
+  and parse usage from that.
+
+### 3. bash tool: command-stream keeps the whole output in memory, and the runner is pinned by an abort listener (high for large outputs)
+
+- Where: `js/src/tool/bash.ts:231-232` and `:296-300`.
+  ```ts
+  const timeoutSignal = AbortSignal.timeout(timeout);           // 60 s default, 10 min max
+  const cancel = AbortSignal.any([ctx.abort, timeoutSignal]);
+  new ProcessRunner(..., { signal: stop?.signal ?? cancel, capture: true, ... })
+  ```
+- Resource, part (a): unbounded buffering. `capture: true` makes
+  command-stream push every stdout and stderr chunk into
+  `runner.outChunks/errChunks`. See command-stream 2.6.0
+  `src/$.process-runner-execution.mjs:291,331`. At exit it also builds
+  `Buffer.concat(...).toString()` (`:461-468`).
+
+  bash.ts carefully keeps only `2 * MAX_BYTES` of output (`:234-249`), but the
+  runner holds the full output twice. A command that prints 500 MB costs about
+  1 GB. bash.ts only reads `command.result.child.signalCode` from the result.
+- Resource, part (b): retention. `setupExternalAbortSignal` (`:545`) adds
+  `signal.addEventListener('abort', () => stopForAbort(runner))` and never
+  removes it. Bun keeps an `AbortSignal.any` dependent that has a listener
+  alive while a source is alive; the `abort-any-retention.ts` experiment showed
+  0/200 closures collected.
+
+  So the runner and its captured buffers outlive the tool call until the
+  timeout fires (60 s to 10 min) or the turn ends. `prompt.ts` aborts the
+  per-loop controller in `cancel()` via `defer`. In a busy turn, every bash call
+  of the last 60 s or more stays resident at once.
+- Growth trigger: every bash tool call (default timeout 60 s).
+- Fix: pass `capture: false`. The tool consumes `command.stream()` chunks
+  itself. Confirm that the `stream()` and `result.child` paths still work with
+  capture off in the pinned version. Also give the runner its own
+  `AbortController`, link it with a listener that bash.ts removes in a
+  `finally`, and abort the private controller in the `finally` so command-stream's
+  listener is released immediately.
+- Version note: `bun.lock` pins command-stream 2.4.0. Only 2.6.0 is in the
+  local Bun cache, so the line numbers above are from 2.6.0. Re-check 2.4.0
+  when node_modules is installed.

+  subagent (task) sessions. It is freed only on `Instance.dispose`. In server
+  mode or a long continuous run with many sessions this grows without bound.
+  The per-entry size is small.

+  of sessions kept (LRU).

+  `sleep(...)`/`continue`.

+### 8. `SessionRetry.sleep` leaves its abort listener attached after the delay elapses (low)
+
+- `js/src/session/retry.ts:130-143`. Called from
+  `js/src/session/processor.ts:805` with the turn's abort signal. Each retry
+  adds a listener (`{ once: true }` only removes it after abort). The listeners
+  are bounded by the retry count and released when the turn ends.
+- Fix: `setTimeout(() => { signal.removeEventListener('abort', onAbort); resolve(); }, ...)`.
+  `retry-fetch.ts:179-216` already does this correctly.
+
+### 9. `withTimeout` keeps the timer when the wrapped promise rejects (low)
+
+- `js/src/util/timeout.ts:4-7`. `clearTimeout` runs only on fulfilment, so a
+  rejected MCP call (`js/src/mcp/index.ts:610-620`) leaves an unref'd timer
+  and its closure alive until the timeout.
+- Fix: use `promise.finally(() => clearTimeout(timeout))`.
+
+### 10. `Instance.dispose()` leaves the directory in `cache` (low)
+
+- `js/src/project/instance.ts:13,58-62`. `dispose()` disposes the state but does
+  not `cache.delete(directory)`, so the resolved `Context` stays. Only
+  `disposeAll()` clears it (`:73`). One entry per directory ever served
+  (server mode with per-request `directory`).
+- Fix: `cache.delete(Instance.directory)` in `dispose()`.
+
+### 11. Pending permission asks are not dropped on session abort (low)
+
+- `js/src/permission/index.ts:383-390`. `pending[sessionID][id]` holds a
+  promise and its resolve and reject functions until answered or until
+  `Instance` is disposed (`:320-330`). An aborted turn that was waiting on
+  `ask` leaves its entry behind.
+- Fix: reject and delete the entries for a session when its abort signal fires
+  (`SessionPrompt.cancel`).
+
+### 12. Server: client disconnect does not cancel the turn (low to medium)
+
+- `js/src/server/server.ts:195-201`. `POST /session/:id/message` awaits
+  `SessionPrompt.prompt` inside `stream()`. When the HTTP client disconnects,
+  the turn, with its LLM stream and tools, keeps running to completion.
+- Fix: `stream.onAbort(() => SessionPrompt.cancel(sessionID))`.
+
+### 13. Optional per-request provider timeout signal (low)
+
+- `js/src/provider/provider.ts:1131-1137`. This is `AbortSignal.any([init.signal,
+  AbortSignal.timeout(t)])` per request, only when a provider `timeout` is
+  configured. The SDK's listeners on it are pinned until the timeout fires.
+  This is the same mechanism as item 3, but no large buffers are attached.
+
+### Rust (`rust/src`)
+
+### R1. bash timeout kills only the shell, not its process tree (medium)
+
+- `rust/src/tool/bash.rs:111-139`. The child is spawned without
+  `process_group(0)`/`setsid`, and `child.kill()` sends SIGKILL to `bash` only.
+  Background or pipeline grandchildren (`cmd &`, `a | b`, servers) survive as
+  orphans after every timed-out call.
+- Second effect: if a grandchild inherits stdout, `pump` never sees EOF after
+  `bash` exits. The call then always waits for the full timeout.
+- Fix: `cmd.process_group(0)` (tokio `Command::process_group`, Unix). On
+  timeout, `libc::killpg(pgid, SIGKILL)`. On Windows, use a job object or
+  `taskkill /T`.
+- Output buffering is fine. `Capture` keeps at most `4 * MAX_BYTES` per stream
+  (`:209-222`).
+
+### R2. Rust grep loads whole files and collects unlimited results (low to medium)
+
+- `rust/src/tool/grep.rs:158-197,204-240`. `collect_files` walks everything
+  except `.git`, with `follow_links(true)` and no `.gitignore` handling. It
+  then runs `fs::read_to_string` on every file, a blocking call on the async
+  runtime. `results` is unbounded unless the caller passes `head_limit`.
+- Fix: default the limit (for example 100 entries, as in JS), skip files over a
+  size cap, honour ignore files (the `ignore` crate), and use
+  `spawn_blocking`.
+
+### R3. Rust read loads the whole file before slicing (low)
+
+- `rust/src/tool/read.rs` (`async_fs::read(&filepath)` after the binary
+  sample). This is a one-off per call, but a multi-GB file is fully
+  materialized.
+- Fix: read with a `BufReader` line by line up to `offset + limit`.
+
+---
+
+## Checked and found OK (not leaks)
+
+- `session/prompt.ts` `state` per session: removed via
+  `using _ = defer(() => cancel(sessionID))`.
+- `session/status.ts`: the entry is deleted on idle.
+- `session/retry.ts` `retryStates`: cleared on finish, on non-retryable errors
+  and on overflow.
+- `tool/task.ts`: the abort listener is removed via `defer`, and Bus `unsub`
+  runs in a `finally`.
+- `tool/webfetch.ts`: bodies are cancelled and `readBounded` caps the read;
+  the timeout signal is not linked to a capturing listener.
+- `file/ripgrep.ts` `files()`: the `finally` cancels the reader, kills rg and
+  awaits exit.
+- `mcp/index.ts`: state dispose closes clients and kills descendants; failed
+  clients are closed in `tools()`.
+- `bus/index.ts` unsubscribe, `util/lock.ts` (empty locks removed),
+  `util/log.ts` (one logger per service), `util/verbose-fetch.ts` (log tee
+  read to the end).
+- `provider/model-discovery.ts` caches: bounded.
+- `provider/retry-fetch.ts` own `sleep` and `createIsolatedRateLimitSignal`:
+  cleaned up in `finally`.
+- `tool/tool.ts` `define`: wrapper accumulation already fixed (see
+  `../bash-web/define-accumulation.ts`).
+- `session/processor.ts:258` calls `MessageV2.parts()` per tool-call event for
+  doom-loop detection. That is CPU and IO per event, not retained memory.

+# Rust tool parity fixes (issue #335)
+
+Follow-up to `js-rust-parity-audit.md` (§6 fix list) and
+`backward-compat-audit.md`. JS is the reference. Every behaviour change
+has a test; where it changes what an earlier Rust release did, a switch
+restores the earlier behaviour and a legacy test covers it. Tests that need
+a switch use `ToolContext::with_settings`, so no test mutates the process
+environment.
+
+## Switches (`rust/src/compat.rs`, flags in `rust/src/cli.rs`)
+
+| Variable | Flag | Restores / sets |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_BASH_SHELL` | `--bash-shell` | `legacy` = `bash -c` |
+| `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_LEGACY_TOOL_OUTPUT` | `--legacy-tool-output` | earlier output text, errors, diff format, truncation |
+| `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_LEGACY_EDIT_MATCHING` | `--legacy-edit-matching` | earlier edit matching (empty oldString overwrite, unguarded block anchor, no BOM handling, no disproportionate refusal) |
+| `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_GLOB_FOLLOW_SYMLINKS` | `--glob-follow-symlinks` | follow symlinks in glob/grep/list |
+| `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_GREP_HIDDEN` | `--grep-hidden` | `false` = skip dotfiles |
+| `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_GREP_TIMEOUT_MS` | `--grep-timeout-ms` | grep time limit |
+| `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_READ_MAX_LINES` / `_READ_MAX_BYTES` | `--read-max-lines` / `--read-max-bytes` | read caps, 0 = none |
+| `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_READ_ONLY` | `--read-only` | JS read-only tool filter |
+| `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_DISABLE_TOOLS` | `--disable-tools` | JS disableTools filter |
+
+The audit proposed separate `EDIT_ALLOW_EMPTY_OLDSTRING`,
+`EDIT_FUZZY_THRESHOLD`, `GLOB_LIMIT` switches; they are folded into
+`LEGACY_EDIT_MATCHING` and `LEGACY_TOOL_OUTPUT`.
+
+## Done (audit §6 numbering)
+
+1. grep: JS listing, `include` alias, rg-style walk (`.gitignore`/`.ignore`,
+   no symlinks, `.git` skipped, binary skipped), time limit, errors.
+2. glob: `rg --files` semantics, absolute paths newest first, 100 limit,
+   "No files found", errors.
+3. todo: JS schema (`cancelled`, `priority`, `id`, optional `activeForm`).
+4. batch: every call past 10 is reported (calls still run sequentially).
+5. Permissions / FileTime: not done, see gaps.
+6. bash: `$SHELL` selection with a POSIX allowlist, stdin `/dev/null`,
+   process-group kill, metadata `timedOut`/`aborted`/`description`.
+7. read: JS line splitting, empty file = 1 line, BOM, NFC names, numeric
+   string params, streaming, caps.
+8. edit: new `rust/src/tool/edit_match.rs` ports the JS replacers in the JS
+   order (best-scoring block anchor at 0.65, disproportionate refusal with
+   the JS error, unique candidate or next replacer, JS `trim`/`\s`
+   whitespace, UTF-16 lengths for the similarity, `\\\n` unescape), BOM
+   split/join, jsdiff `createTwoFilesPatch` + `trimDiff` diff (4 lines of
+   context, as the jsdiff default), `filediff` with the file's own line
+   endings, JS errors for missing file, directory and empty `filePath`.
+   Reference outputs were generated with the JS code and the `diff`
+   package and are asserted in `rust/tests/tool_edit.rs`.
+9. list: JS ignore globs, `.gitignore`/`.ignore`, no truncation note,
+   JS errors and title.
+10. webfetch: script/style with attributes, JS status/timeout text,
+    `text/markdown;q=0.7`, non-ASCII-safe tag removal.
+11. CLI: `--read-only`, `--disable-tools` and the env vars (registry
+    filter, batch rejects them).
+12. Latent bugs: `permission.rs` non-ASCII panic, `Filesystem::contains`
+    prefix fallback, id panic on `""`.
+13. websearch: `numResults: 0` = 8, enum validation.
+14. Docs: `rust/README.md` tool list and switch table; changelog fragment
+    `rust/changelog.d/20261103_002356_tool_js_parity_and_compat_switches.md`.
+
+write needed no change: BOM handling, metadata and "Wrote file
+successfully." already match JS.
+
+## Deliberate divergences
+
+- edit: the replacers run on the LF view of the file and the result is
+  mapped back with `restore_line_endings`; JS converts oldString/newString
+  to the dominant ending. Equal for pure LF/CRLF files; Rust also keeps
+  the untouched lines of a mixed file.
+- edit: an empty candidate (e.g. a whitespace-only oldString after
+  trimming) is skipped. JS would accept `""` and `String.replace` would
+  insert newString at the start of the file.
+- edit/write descriptions keep the Rust text, because the JS `edit.txt`
+  and `write.txt` require a prior read that Rust does not enforce.
+- bash: default timeout 2 min (JS 1 min) and stdout/stderr joined with
+  `--- stderr ---` (JS interleaves); `aborted` is always `false` (no
+  abort signal reaches a tool in the CLI).
+- codesearch: `tokensNum` is clamped to 1000..=50000 instead of rejected.
+- webfetch: markdown conversion is a small converter, not Turndown;
+  output differs in details.
+- glob/list skip `.git` at any depth; JS passes `--glob=!.git/*` to rg
+  (grep already uses `!**/.git/**` in JS, so grep matches).
+- grep: the binary check scans the whole file for NUL while streaming
+  (rg looks at a prefix and then per buffer).
+- legacy glob output keeps the 100 result limit.
+
+## Remaining gaps (not faked)
+
+- FileTime (read-before-edit assert, read stamps) and the per-file edit
+  lock (audit X6, §6 item 5) are not implemented. The Rust CLI has no
+  session: each invocation is a separate process, and `batch` runs its
+  calls one after another, so a lock would never be contended and a
+  read stamp could not survive between invocations. Documented in
+  `rust/src/tool/edit.rs` and `rust/README.md`.
+- Permissions (audit X5): `permission.rs` is still not consulted by the
+  tools; the CLI never executes tools from a model, so there is no
+  ask/approve loop to hook into.
+- Cross-cutting X1-X3: serde defaults vs raw JS args, the `AgentError`
+  wrapper text and `join` without `..` normalisation remain, except
+  where a tool now coerces numeric strings (read) or uses the JS message.
+- edit: a non-UTF-8 file still fails to read.
+- multiedit: `edits: []` returns empty output (JS throws a TypeError).
+- The Rust CLI does not call an LLM and does not emit the JS event
+  envelope (audit §3).

+---
+'@link-assistant/agent': patch
+---
+
+fix: sync reliability fixes for existing tools, the session loop, providers and MCP from upstream OpenCode (#335)
+
+- `edit` and `write` serialize changes to the same file, so parallel edits no
+  longer overwrite each other (upstream #4388, #23483).
+- `edit` no longer replaces unrelated code through loose fuzzy matching, and
+  an empty `oldString` no longer overwrites an existing file (upstream #30932).
+- `edit` keeps CRLF, mixed line endings and a UTF-8 BOM; `write` keeps the
+  BOM (upstream #9443, #53166, #23797).
+- `replaceAll` inserts `$&`, `$1` and similar text literally.
+- The "modified since read" check compares file mtime and size instead of
+  clocks, and treats equivalent paths as one file (upstream #17835, #20367).
+- `edit` works right after `write`, and both return a short confirmation.
+- `read` resolves relative paths against the session directory, caps output
+  at 50 KB and 2000 lines, handles CRLF files, directories and file names
+  with macOS narrow no-break spaces or curly quotes, and samples only 4 KB
+  for the binary check.
+- `grep` keeps matches when some paths are unreadable (rg exit 2), searches
+  hidden files except `.git`, honours aborts, times out after 30 s, and
+  reports invalid regexes and missing paths clearly.
+- `glob` and `ls` no longer hang after their 100-result limit, stop rg on
+  abort, do not follow symlinked directories, and ignore a user ripgrep
+  config.
+- `bash` runs commands in `$SHELL` or bash instead of `/bin/sh`, keeps the
+  end of long output (where errors are), never splits UTF-8 characters,
+  bounds the live metadata preview, frees parser trees, and asks for
+  permission for write redirects in read-only/plan modes.
+- `webfetch`, `websearch` and `codesearch` enforce the 5 MB limit while
+  streaming, time out with a clear message, retry Cloudflare challenges with
+  an honest user agent, accept plain JSON or SSE replies from Exa, and pass
+  `EXA_API_KEY` when set; `webfetch` defaults to markdown.
+- Tools no longer stack a new execute wrapper on every init, and `task`
+  always unsubscribes from child-session events.
+- A prompt that exceeds the context window (400 "prompt is too long", 413,
+  mid-stream `context_length_exceeded`) compacts the session and carries on
+  instead of ending it; a second overflow stops with a clear error
+  (upstream #6480, #14707).
+- Tool calls reported with finish reason `stop` still get their results sent
+  back to the model (upstream #14973).
+- Retryable 5xx stream errors, plain-text rate limits, Vertex
+  `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, OpenAI item 404s and truncated gzip bodies are
+  retried; retry delays never exceed the `setTimeout` limit; API errors
+  include the body's message.
+- A `retry-after` longer than the retry timeout now stops the turn instead of
+  starting another step, and retry-only errors can be saved on a message.
+- Interrupted tools keep their start time and partial output and are marked
+  `interrupted`; non-object tool input is stored as `{ value }`; tool events
+  that arrive without `tool-input-start` are kept.
+- Lone UTF-16 surrogates, empty Anthropic/Bedrock parts and empty user
+  messages are no longer sent; provider signatures and reasoning from another
+  model are not replayed; prompt caching merges provider options deeply and
+  uses Bedrock's cache-point format; Moonshot/Kimi tool schemas are fixed.
+- Reasoning tokens are no longer charged twice, and the Anthropic thinking
+  budget is kept within the model's output limit.
+- MCP: connect and `tools/list` time out, list pagination is bounded,
+  servers are listed in parallel, failed clients are closed and reported as
+  `failed` (also for invalid URLs), servers without tools stay connected,
+  results without `content` are normalized, a timed-out call is really
+  aborted, per-tool timeouts work for server names with `_`, the connect
+  timeout is no longer `NaN`, and dispose stops grandchild processes.
+- `cancel()` rejects queued callers with an `AbortError`.
+- Memory: the SSE usage map is bounded, the usage tee branch is always read to
+  the end, retried 5xx/429 bodies are cancelled, retry sleeps and grep/bash
+  drop their abort listeners, `withTimeout` clears its timer on rejection,
+  disposed instances leave the cache, cancelled turns reject their pending
+  permission asks, and deleting a session drops its file read stamps.
+- Continuous and single-shot modes no longer wait forever for `session.idle`
+  when a prompt fails before its loop starts.
+- MCP servers accept `connect_timeout`; `timeout` keeps its previous meaning
+  (listing tools). Credentials in MCP and provider URLs are masked in verbose
+  logs.
+- The default model and default compaction model are now
+  `kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (1M context), and the default compaction
+  cascade is `(kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free kilo/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free same)`,
+  because Kilo withdrew Nemotron 3 Super. `kilo/nemotron-3-super-free` (and the
+  bare `nemotron-3-super-free`) stays accepted as a deprecated alias that runs
+  on `kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free` and logs one warning naming the
+  replacement. The free-model drift check skips deprecated aliases and
+  requires every alias target to be a built-in model.
+- Git worktrees and submodules no longer crash the CLI: the project id cache
+  was written to `.git/opencode` while `.git` is a file there, and the
+  unhandled ENOTDIR rejection ended the process. The id is now cached in the
+  common git directory (as upstream does), and a failed cache write is only
+  logged.
+- npm dependencies are refreshed to their latest releases (the `ai` SDK and
+  every `@ai-sdk/*` provider, `@agentclientprotocol/sdk`,
+  `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `@opencode-ai/sdk`, `@opentui/*` 0.8,
+  `command-stream`, `hono`, `remeda`, `google-auth-library`, `glob` 14,
+  `minimatch` 11 and the rest). `solid-js` is no longer pinned and the
+  obsolete `seroval` override is dropped. `lino-arguments` stays on 0.3.x:
+  0.4.0 throws "Ambiguous environment aliases" at startup when both spellings
+  of a variable are set (for example `http_proxy` and `HTTP_PROXY`).
+
+Backward compatibility: every user-visible change can be reverted with an
+option (each also has a `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env var): `--bash-shell legacy`,
+`--legacy-tool-output`, `--legacy-edit-matching`, `--glob-follow-symlinks`,
+`--no-grep-hidden`, `--grep-timeout-ms 0`, `--read-max-lines 0`,
+`--read-max-bytes 0`, `--legacy-error-names`, `--legacy-token-usage`,
+`--legacy-loop-exit` and `--mcp-connect-timeout 0`.
